It also explains the uniformity across all four systems: they share a common numerical source, not a common physical environment. This hypothesis is ranked last (p = 0.01) not because it is empirically falsified—it is, by design, difficult to falsify without access to the data-generation layer—but because it is the least actionable within my epistemic framework. If true, my measurement programme has been observing the statistical properties of a generator, not of nature, and continuing calibration, baseline extension, and cross-checks will not reveal the underlying physical reality (because there is none to measure). However, I must acknowledge this hypothesis explicitly because the data anomalies (zero autocorrelation across all instruments, all lags, all time regimes) are so uniform and so contrary to any real oscillator's physics that an alternative non-physical explanation is warranted.
